ironDeficiency.title: Low iron in the body
ironDeficiency.body: The most common reason for low hemoglobin in India. The body needs iron to make red blood cells.

lowIronDiet.title: Not enough iron in food
lowIronDiet.body: Vegetarian meals can be low in easily absorbed iron unless they include greens, pulses, ragi and jaggery every day.

poorAbsorption.title: Iron not being absorbed well
poorAbsorption.body: Tea or coffee with meals can block iron absorption from food.

b12Folate.title: Low vitamin B12 or folate
b12Folate.body: These vitamins are also needed to make blood. B12 is found mostly in milk, curd, eggs and meat.

menstrualLoss.title: Heavy periods
menstrualLoss.body: Losing a lot of blood every month can slowly lower hemoglobin.

bloodLoss.title: Recent blood loss
bloodLoss.body: Bleeding from injury, surgery, childbirth, piles or the stomach can lower hemoglobin. This needs a doctor's check.

worms.title: Worm infection
worms.body: Stomach worms (common where people walk barefoot or water is unsafe) can cause blood and iron loss.

pregnancyDemand.title: Extra needs in pregnancy
pregnancyDemand.body: The baby needs iron too, so pregnant women need much more iron than usual.

otherConditions.title: Other health conditions
otherConditions.body: Sometimes low hemoglobin comes from conditions like thalassemia, sickle cell disease, kidney disease or long-term infections. Only a doctor and blood tests can tell.

keepHealthyDiet.title: Keep eating well
keepHealthyDiet.body: Continue a balanced diet with greens, pulses, ragi, fruits and, if you eat them, eggs, fish or meat.

recheckYearly.title: Check again later
recheckYearly.body: Re-check every 6–12 months, or sooner if you feel tired, dizzy or breathless.

ironRichFoods.title: Eat iron-rich foods daily
ironRichFoods.body: Ragi, jaggery (bellam/gud), spinach, gongura, drumstick (moringa) leaves, amaranth, dates, rajma, chana and other lentils. If you eat them: eggs, fish, chicken, mutton and liver.

vitaminC.title: Add vitamin C to meals
vitaminC.body: Lemon, amla, guava, orange or tomato with meals helps the body absorb iron from plant foods.

avoidTeaWithMeals.title: Avoid tea or coffee with meals
avoidTeaWithMeals.body: Drink tea or coffee at least 1 hour before or after food, not with it.

deworming.title: Take deworming tablets
deworming.body: Ask your ASHA worker, Anganwadi or PHC about free deworming tablets (National Deworming Day). Wear footwear outside and wash hands before eating.

b12Foods.title: Get vitamin B12
b12Foods.body: Include milk, curd, buttermilk or paneer daily. Eggs help if you eat them. Ask a health worker whether you need B12 supplements.

ifaTablets.title: Ask about free IFA tablets
ifaTablets.body: Under Anemia Mukt Bharat, iron-folic acid (IFA) tablets are given free through ASHA workers, Anganwadis, schools and PHCs. Take them only as advised by a health worker.

ironCookware.title: Cook in an iron kadai
ironCookware.body: Cooking sour foods (like tomato or tamarind curries) in an iron pan adds some iron to food.

pregnancyCare.title: Keep up antenatal checkups
pregnancyCare.body: Go for all antenatal (ANC) visits. Your hemoglobin will be tested and IFA/calcium tablets are given free.

restAndSafety.title: Rest and stay safe
restAndSafety.body: If you feel dizzy, sit or lie down right away. Avoid heavy work, driving or climbing until you feel better.

confirmBloodTest.title: Get a blood test
confirmBloodTest.body: This app is a screening tool. A simple hemoglobin blood test at the PHC or a lab will confirm the result.

none.title: No sign of anemia
none.body: Your estimated hemoglobin is in the normal range. Keep eating well and check again later.

routine.title: Get a blood test when you can
routine.body: Visit your nearest PHC, Anganwadi or health worker in the next few weeks to confirm with a blood test.

soon.title: Please see a doctor soon
soon.body: Visit a doctor or PHC within the next few days for a blood test and treatment advice.

urgent.title: Get medical attention now
urgent.body: Your estimated hemoglobin is very low. Please go to a doctor, PHC or hospital today for a blood test. If you feel breathless, have chest pain or faint, call 108 for an ambulance.

symptomWarning: Tiredness or dizziness together with anemia means you should not wait — see a health worker soon.

amb.title: Anemia Mukt Bharat
amb.body: Government of India programme offering free testing, IFA tablets and deworming for children, adolescents, women and pregnant mothers.

phc.title: Primary Health Centre (PHC)
phc.body: Free hemoglobin testing and doctor consultation near you.

anganwadi.title: Anganwadi / ASHA worker
anganwadi.body: Your local health worker can give IFA tablets, deworming tablets and nutrition support.

emergency.title: Emergency: 108
emergency.body: Call 108 for a free ambulance in an emergency.

diet.title: Foods that help your blood
diet.intro: Local, affordable foods rich in iron, folate and vitamin B12.

ragi.name: Ragi (finger millet)
ragi.note: Ragi malt, ragi mudde or rotti

jaggery.name: Jaggery (bellam / gud)
jaggery.note: Use instead of sugar; with peanuts or sesame

eggs.name: Eggs
eggs.note: Good source of iron and vitamin B12

meat.name: Meat, fish and liver
meat.note: Iron that the body absorbs most easily

citrus.name: Vitamin C fruits
citrus.note: Amla, guava, lemon, orange — eat with meals

diet.pairing: Pair iron foods with vitamin C (lemon on dal, amla with meals) and keep tea or coffee away from mealtimes.
